title: Journey to the Deep: A Short History of Underwater Exploration
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界奇妙而有趣的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going on a journey to the bottom of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 我是阿拉斯泰尔·布多（Alastair Budge），今天我们要开启一段海底之旅。

sentences.en: Or rather, we aren’t going on a journey, but we will be talking about the fascinating history of humans trying to travel underwater and understand what lies beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 或者确切地说，我们不是真的去旅行，而是要探讨人类尝试在水下航行并了解水面之下的精彩历史。

sentences.en: It’s an amazing tale of bravery, marvellous inventions, strange creatures, and as we will discover, it is a story that has barely even got started.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于勇敢、奇妙发明和奇异生物的惊人故事，而且正如我们将发现的那样，这个故事才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s not waste a minute and learn about the history of underwater exploration.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们一分钟也不要浪费，一起来了解水下探索的历史吧。

sentences.en: For as long as we humans have walked on the land, we have also built boats, canoes, and rafts to travel on water.
sentences.zh: 自从我们人类在陆地上行走以来，我们也建造了船只、独木舟和木筏来在水上航行。

sentences.en: People have explored rivers, lakes and seas, crossed oceans to far off lands.
sentences.zh: 人们探索了河流、湖泊和海洋，跨越海洋去往遥远的陆地。

sentences.en: The seas and oceans have always been a subject of intrigue and mystery, with their storms, high waves, and strange creatures that lurk beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 由于狂风暴雨、滔天巨浪和潜伏在水面之下的奇异生物，海洋和大海一直是阴谋和神秘的主题。

sentences.en: In practically every culture with some history of seafaring, there are stories of mysterious sea monsters, beasts from the deep.
sentences.zh: 在几乎所有拥有航海历史的文化中，都有关于神秘海怪和深渊野兽的故事。

sentences.en: After all, it is hardly surprising. People knew that there were animals down there, because they could throw nets or hooks into the sea and pull them out.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这并不令人意外。人们知道水里有动物，因为他们可以把网或鱼钩扔进海里并把它们拉上来。

sentences.en: Fish, octopus, squid, sharks, whales, creatures of all shapes and sizes.
sentences.zh: 鱼类、章鱼、乌贼、鲨鱼、鲸鱼，各种形状和大小的生物。

sentences.en: Clearly, there was an abundance of life beneath the surface, but compared to the life on earth, the ocean, and its inhabitants, were very poorly understood.
sentences.zh: 很明显，水面之下有着丰富的生命，但与陆地上的生命相比，海洋及其居民受到的了解却非常少。

sentences.en: For starters, for thousands of years there was not even agreement on whether the deep sea ever “finished”, whether there was a floor to the ocean, or whether it was an eternal abyss of water.
sentences.zh: 首先，几千年来，人们甚至无法就深海是否“有尽头”、海洋是否有海底，或者它是否是一个永恒的水渊达成共识。

sentences.en: After all, you couldn’t see the bottom and there was no possibility of going there.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，你看不到海底，也不可能去到那里。

sentences.en: So did the sea continue forever, or not?
sentences.zh: 所以大海是永远延伸下去，还是并非如此？

sentences.en: In 1521, a man called Ferdinand Magellan did attempt to answer this question.
sentences.zh: 1521年，一个叫斐迪南·麦哲伦（Ferdinand Magellan）的人确实试图回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Now, you might know about Ferdinand Magellan already, or you might remember him from Episode 196.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能已经知道斐迪南·麦哲伦，或者你可能在第196集里对他的印象深刻。

sentences.en: Long story short, he was a Portuguese explorer and the first person to sail all the way around the world.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，他是一位葡萄牙探险家，也是第一个环游世界的人。

sentences.en: Well, whether it was actually Magellan or someone else is another question that you can hear about more in that episode, but the point is that he was an explorer who was the first or one of the first people to ever sail all the way around the world.
sentences.zh: 好吧，究竟是麦哲伦还是其他人，那是你可以在那一集里了解到的另一个问题，但重点是他是第一个或最早环游世界的探险家之一。

sentences.en: Anyway, in 1521 he was a couple of years into his expedition, and he was in the middle of the vast Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，在1521年，他的远征已经进行了好几年，当时他正身处浩瀚的太平洋中央。

sentences.en: He attempted to answer the question of the ocean’s depth.
sentences.zh: 他试图回答海洋深度的问题。

sentences.en: How he did this was by attaching a cannonball to a piece of long rope, and then lowering it off the side of the boat.
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做的呢？他把一个加农炮弹绑在一根长绳子上，然后把它从船边放下去。

sentences.en: As the men lowered the cannonball, they measured how much rope had been used, with the idea that when the rope went slack, when the line was no longer tight, this meant that the cannonball had hit the bottom.
sentences.zh: 当船员们放下炮弹时，他们测量了用去了多少绳子，其原理是当绳子变松、不再紧绷时，这就意味着炮弹已经触底了。

sentences.en: The men lowered and lowered and lowered it, but after 732 metres it was still just as tight as before.
sentences.zh: 船员们不断地往下放、往下放、往下放，但在732米之后，它依然像以前一样紧绷。

sentences.en: And they had run out of rope. Magellan concluded that, and I’m quoting directly, the ocean was “immeasurably deep”, too deep to be measured.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的绳子用光了。麦哲伦得出结论，我直接引用他的话，海洋是“不可测的深”，深得无法测量。

sentences.en: This might sound like a relatively basic way of measuring the depth of a body of water, but it works very well, and had been the way in which people measured the depth of water for thousands of years, and it was still the main way people measured depth for much of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是测量水体深度的一种相对基础的方法，但它非常有效，几千年来人们一直用这种方法来测量水深，在20世纪的大部分时间里，它仍然是人们测量深度的主要方法。

sentences.en: Now, of course there is a big difference between knowing how deep a body of water is and knowing what is actually going on beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 当然，知道一个水体有多深和知道水面之下到底发生了什么，这两者有着巨大的区别。

sentences.en: To state the obvious, there is a hard limit of how deep a human can dive below the surface on their own, without any kind of assistance.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，人类在没有任何辅助的情况下，自己能潜入水下的深度是有一个硬性极限的。

sentences.en: Just going down 10 metres below the surface doubles the pressure upon the body, which is why you feel that discomfort in your ears, and why you need to blow, holding your nose to equalise the pressure if you are diving.
sentences.zh: 仅仅下潜到水面以下10米，身体承受的压力就会加倍，这就是为什么你会感到耳朵不舒服，也是为什么如果你在潜水，你需要捏着鼻子吹气来平衡压力。

sentences.en: So there’s the question of pressure, but there’s also the more important question of running out of breath.
sentences.zh: 所以存在压力的问题，但也有一个更重要的问题，那就是憋气。

sentences.en: Even the most seasoned divers, people from communities where they would dive for pearls or sponges, they can typically only get to depths of 20 or 30 metres, and hold their breath for around 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 即使是最经验丰富的潜水员，来自那些以潜水采珠或海绵为生的社区的人，他们通常也只能达到20或30米的深度，并且只能憋气大约10分钟。

sentences.en: Sure, that is very impressive, but it really is only a tiny fraction of the depth of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 当然，这非常令人印象深刻，但它真的只是海洋深度的一小部分。

sentences.en: And even going back thousands of years, people knew what they needed to explore the deep: some kind of container and a source of air.
sentences.zh: 即使追溯到几千年来，人们也知道他们探索深海需要什么：某种容器和氧气来源。

sentences.en: One of the first mentions of this kind of contraption dates back to Aristotle in the 4th Century BC, but this was just from a theoretical perspective, there is no evidence that any such object was ever built.
sentences.zh: 这种玩意的最早记载之一可以追溯到公元前4世纪的亚里士多德，但这只是从理论角度出发的，没有证据表明曾经建造过这样的东西。

sentences.en: Yet, the idea captured imaginations for centuries to come.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个想法在接下来的几个世纪里激发了人们的想象力。

sentences.en: By the Middle Ages, tales from French and German poetry spoke of a hero using a ‘ diving bell’ to explore the ocean’s depths.
sentences.zh: 到了中世纪，法国和德国诗歌中的故事讲述了一位英雄利用“潜水钟”来探索海洋深处。

sentences.en: One of the most famous legends linked this invention to Alexander the Great, who supposedly descended underwater in a glass bell alongside a few animal companions —a dog, a cat, and even a chicken.
sentences.zh: 最著名的传说之一将这项发明与亚历山大大帝联系在一起，据称他曾和一个动物伙伴——一只狗、一只猫甚至一只鸡——一起乘着玻璃钟潜入水下。

sentences.en: While there’s no historical proof that Alexander attempted such a dive, the story has persisted, blending myth and ambition in the pursuit of the deep.
sentences.zh: 虽然没有历史证据表明亚历山大曾尝试过这样的潜水，但这个故事一直流传下来，在追求深海的过程中将神话与雄心融合在了一起。

sentences.en: The first use of what we now call a diving bell came much later, in the 16th century, invented by the Italian Guglielmo de Lorena.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所说的潜水钟的首次使用要晚得多，在16世纪，由意大利人古列尔莫·德洛雷纳（Guglielmo de Lorena）发明。

sentences.en: Together with a colleague, Francesco De Marchi, de Lorena sought to go to the bottom of Lake Nemi, just to the south of Rome.
sentences.zh: 德洛雷纳与同事弗朗切斯科·德马基（Francesco De Marchi）一起，试图前往位于罗马正南方的内米湖（Lake Nemi）湖底。

sentences.en: At the bottom of this lake lay two huge ancient barges that had been built as floating palaces for the Roman Emperor Caligula in the first century AD.
sentences.zh: 在这个湖底躺着两艘巨大的古代驳船，它们是公元1世纪为罗马皇帝卡利古拉（Caligula）建造的水上宫殿。

sentences.en: They most probably couldn’t be seen from the surface, but there were plenty of historical records and local stories.
sentences.zh: 它们很可能从水面上看不到，但有大量的历史记录和当地的故事。

sentences.en: People knew they were there, only 18 metres below the surface, but this was sufficiently far down that people couldn’t dive and properly explore them.
sentences.zh: 人们知道它们在那里，就在水面以下18米处，但这已经足够深了，人们无法潜水并对它们进行适当的探索。

sentences.en: However, Guglielmo de Lorena invented a device that allowed him to spend hours at a time exploring the ships, meaning he could return to the surface with treasures from ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 然而，古列尔莫·德洛雷纳发明了一种装置，使他能够一次花上几个小时探索这些船只，这意味着他可以带着古罗马的宝藏浮出水面。

sentences.en: Now, how this device actually worked is still a bit of a mystery, because his diving partner, De Marchi, the man who later wrote an account of the adventure, took a vow of secrecy.
sentences.zh: 至于这个装置实际上是如何工作的，现在仍然是个谜，因为他的潜水搭档德马基（后来写下这段冒险经历的人）发誓要保守秘密。

sentences.en: What we know is that it was basically a large wooden barrel with a small piece of crystal for a window.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，它基本上是一个大木桶，带有一小块水晶作为窗户。

sentences.en: This would be put on the diver’s head, and there must have been some way of getting the exhaled air out of the bell and pumping fresh air into it, but as the writer was sworn to secrecy, we don’t know exactly how this was achieved.
sentences.zh: 这会被放在潜水员的头上，一定有某种方法把呼出的气体排出钟外，并将新鲜空气泵入其中，但由于作者发誓保密，我们不知道这是具体如何实现的。

sentences.en: But we know that it worked, there is little doubt about this.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道它管用，这一点几乎毫无疑问。

sentences.en: In fact, in his account, De Marchi would write that the limit to how long a diver could stay underwater with this invention was nothing to do with how much air there was left, but rather how long the diver could withstand the cold of the water and the fatigue of wearing this heavy contraption on their head.
sentences.zh: 事实上，德马基在记述中写道，潜水员使用这项发明在水下停留时间的限制，与剩余多少空气无关，而是取决于潜水员能忍受多久的水温寒冷，以及头上戴着这个沉重装置的疲劳程度。

sentences.en: It was a cunning system indeed, and did allow these men to complete what has been described as one of the first instances of underwater archaeology.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个巧妙的系统，确实让这些人完成了被描述为水下考古最早实例之一的任务。

sentences.en: But, it had its limits. 20 metres, after all, is not very deep.
sentences.zh: 但是，它也有它的局限性。毕竟，20米并不是很深。

sentences.en: Throughout the 16th, 17th and 18th centuries, inventors continued to tinker away on new versions of this technology, trying to solve the problem of how to get rid of exhaled air, have enough capacity for fresh air, and maintain the right pressure at the same time.
sentences.zh: 在16、17和18世纪，发明家们继续摆弄这项技术的新版本，试图解决如何排除呼出的气体、拥有足够的新鲜空气容量以及同时维持正确压力的难题。

sentences.en: And they weren’t doing this only out of scientific curiosity, or out of an innate desire to understand the marine biology of the seas.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做不仅仅是出于对科学的好奇，也不是出于对了解海洋生物学的内在渴望。

sentences.en: The major objective was allowing people to dive down and recover valuables from shipwrecks.
sentences.zh: 主要目标是让人类能够潜入水下并从沉船中打捞贵重物品。

sentences.en: By this point in time, there were hundreds of known shipwrecks with valuable treasure, from ancient Roman shipwrecks through to ships that had only sunk the previous year.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，有数百艘已知的沉船携带着宝贵的财富，从古罗马沉船到刚刚在前一年沉没的船只。

sentences.en: In some cases they were known to contain today’s equivalent of tens of millions of Euros worth of perfectly usable gold, it was just a question of being able to get down there and pick it up.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，已知它们含有相当于今天数千万欧元价值的完全可用的黄金，问题只是在于能否潜下去并把它捡起来。

sentences.en: And with this very real monetary incentive, diving bell technology did increase dramatically, and divers were able to go down to depths of twenty or so metres and stay there for extended periods of time, supported either by tubes or sealed buckets of fresh air delivered from the surface.
sentences.zh: 随着这种非常现实的金钱激励，潜水钟技术有了显著的提高，潜水员能够下潜到二十米左右的深度并在那里停留很长时间，由从水面输送的管道或密封的新鲜空气桶提供支持。

sentences.en: But in 1620, just under 100 years after de Lorena and De Marchi’s trip to the bottom of Lake Nemi, a Dutch inventor named Cornelis Drebbel would design something that would go on to surpass the diving bell: the submarine.
sentences.zh: 但在1620年，就在德洛雷纳和德马基内米湖之行不到100年后，一位名叫科内利斯·德雷贝尔（Cornelis Drebbel）的荷兰发明家设计出了一种将超越潜水钟的东西：潜艇。

sentences.en: He was working in London at the time, having been contracted by the British to work on all sorts of weird and wonderful inventions that might aid the British navy, and the design for a submarine was one of them.
sentences.zh: 他当时在伦敦工作，受英国人委托从事各种可能协助英国海军的古怪而奇妙的发明，潜艇的设计就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Now, his submarine was very different from modern submarines.
sentences.zh: 现在，他的潜艇与现代潜艇截然不同。

sentences.en: It was made of wood and leather, it had oars to propel it, and air was supplied by two tubes that went up to the surface.
sentences.zh: 它是用木头和皮革制成的，有桨来推进，空气则通过通往水面的两根管子供应。

sentences.en: But it worked, sort of. He continually improved the machine, building bigger and better versions of it.
sentences.zh: 但它成功了，某种程度上。他不断改进这台机器，建造了更大、更好的版本。

sentences.en: By the time he had finished, it was able to travel all the way from Westminster to Greenwich in London, a distance of more than 10 kilometres.
sentences.zh: 等他完成时，它已经能够一路从伦敦的威斯敏斯特（Westminster）行驶到格林威治（Greenwich），距离超过10公里。

sentences.en: Underwater, I should add. It travelled at a depth of 4 metres, and he even took King James I of England for a spin, giving him the unusual title of being the first ever monarch to travel underwater.
sentences.zh: 是在水下，我得补充一下。它以4米的深度行驶，他甚至带了英国国王詹姆斯一世（King James I）兜风，赋予了他有史以来第一位在水下旅行君主的独特称号。

sentences.en: Now, unfortunately for Drebbel, the submarine was not considered to have any practical military value, so the project was scrapped, but it was an important development in underwater technology.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，对德雷贝尔来说，这艘潜艇被认为没有任何实际的军事价值，所以这个项目被取消了，但它是水下技术发展中的一个重要里程碑。

sentences.en: The next important step came a century and a half later, during the American war of independence, when an American inventor called David Bushnell created the “Turtle”.
sentences.zh: 下一个重要步骤发生在一个半世纪后，即美国独立战争期间，当时一位名叫大卫·布什内尔（David Bushnell）的美国发明家创造了“海龟号”（Turtle）。

sentences.en: This was a sort of large wooden ball, 3 metres long and 2 metres wide, which could fit one person inside.
sentences.zh: 这是一种类似大木球的东西，长3米，宽2米，里面可以容纳一个人。

sentences.en: Importantly, it was self-powered, so the person inside could pedal with their feet, like a bicycle, to move the submarine forwards.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，它是自驱动的，所以里面的人可以用脚像骑自行车一样踩踏板，来推动潜艇前进。

sentences.en: Its objective was a military one. Remember, this was an American invention created during the American War of Independence.
sentences.zh: 它的目标是军事上的。记住，这是美国独立战争期间发明的美国发明。

sentences.en: The idea was to creep up, undetected, on British ships and plant a bomb on the ship’s hull, the side of the ship, and then rush away before the bomb exploded.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是悄悄地、不被察觉地靠近英国船只，在船体即船的侧面安放一枚炸弹，然后在炸弹爆炸前迅速逃离。

sentences.en: It was a similar idea to a submarine firing a torpedo, but the main difference being that it had to pedal up to the ship with the bomb and stick it to the side, rather than firing it from a distance of several hundred metres or even kilometres.
sentences.zh: 这与潜艇发射鱼雷的想法相似，但主要的区别在于，它必须踩着踏板带着炸弹靠近船只并把它贴在侧面，而不是从几百米甚至几公里的距离外发射。

sentences.en: It sounded perfectly good in theory, but in practice it never actually worked.
sentences.zh: 这在理论上听起来非常完美，但在实践中却从未真正成功过。

sentences.en: The currents were too strong, so it got pushed around too much, and it couldn’t hold enough air to stay underwater for long enough, so it never actually completed a successful mission.
sentences.zh: 水流太强了，所以它被推来推去，而且它无法容纳足够的空气在水下呆足够长的时间，所以它从来没有真正完成过一次成功的任务。

sentences.en: Fast forward to the late 19th century, and submarine technology had improved dramatically.
sentences.zh: 快进到19世纪末，潜水艇技术已经有了显着的改进。

sentences.en: And with the invention of the torpedo, the submarine became a viable and deadly military asset.
sentences.zh: 随着鱼雷的发明，潜艇成为了一种可行且致命的军事资产。

sentences.en: But these submarines still weren’t able to go particularly deep, not much more than a couple of hundred metres, and what’s more, we are talking about deep-sea exploration, not warfare here.
sentences.zh: 但这些潜艇仍然不能去到特别深的地方，最多也就两百米左右，而且我们要说的是深海探索，而不是这里的战争。

sentences.en: At the same time as submarine technology was going through a period of rapid development, there was a greater desire to understand the seas and oceans from a scientific perspective.
sentences.zh: 在潜水艇技术经历快速发展时期的同时，从科学角度理解海洋的渴望也更加强烈。

sentences.en: Between the years of 1872 and 1876, a British ship called HMS Challenger embarked on a huge mission of scientific exploration, travelling a grand total of 127,580 kilometres, the equivalent of going around the world more than three times.
sentences.zh: 在1872年至1876年期间，一艘名为“挑战者号”（HMS Challenger）的英国船只踏上了科学探索的宏大任务，总行程达127,580公里，相当于环游世界三圈以上。

sentences.en: The objective was to understand the seas and oceans, and it was tasked with measuring the depth of the ocean, which it did 492 times, taking samples from the bottom of the ocean, which it did 133 times, pulling huge nets through the water to see what lay beneath, which it did 151 times, and measuring the temperature of the water, which it did 263 times.
sentences.zh: 其目标是了解海洋，它的任务是测量海洋深度（进行了492次），从海底取样（进行了133次），将巨型网拖过水面以查看水下有什么（进行了151次），以及测量水温（进行了263次）。

sentences.en: It was a gargantuan mission, and it was hugely important in the growing field of oceanography, the science of the sea.
sentences.zh: 这是一项庞大的任务，在不断发展的海洋学领域具有极其重要的意义。

sentences.en: To those who had thought the deep sea was inhospitable, unable to sustain life, they were proved to be wholly mistaken.
sentences.zh: 对于那些曾认为深海不适宜居住、无法维持生命的人来说，事实证明他们完全错了。

sentences.en: In its four year voyage, the Challenger discovered around 4,700 new species of marine life.
sentences.zh: 在其四年的航行中，“挑战者号”发现了大约4,700种新的海洋生物。

sentences.en: The crew also discovered the deepest place on Earth, or at least, the deepest-known place on Earth.
sentences.zh: 船员们还发现了地球上最深的地方，或者至少是人类所知的地球最深处。

sentences.en: While in the Pacific Ocean they conducted one of their 492 depth samples, dropping a lead weight to the bottom and continuing to let the rope down until it hit the bottom, pretty much like Magellan did 350 years before.
sentences.zh: 在太平洋航行时，他们进行了492次深度采样之一，将铅锤扔到海底，并继续放绳子直到它撞击海底，这几乎就像350年前麦哲伦做的那样。

sentences.en: They continued for 8,184 metres before the rope went slack, indicating that the bottom had been hit.
sentences.zh: 他们一直下放了8,184米，直到绳子变松，表明已经触底。

sentences.en: What they had found was part of what we now call the Mariana Trench, the deepest ocean trench in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们发现的是我们现在所说的马里亚纳海沟（Mariana Trench）的一部分，这是世界上最深的海洋海沟。

sentences.en: Now, they didn’t actually find the deepest bit of the trench, the deepest known part is actually 10,984 metres deep, making it more than 2,000 metres further from the Earth’s surface than the peak of Mount Everest.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们实际上并没有找到海沟最深的部分，已知最深的部分其实深达10,984米，这使得它比珠穆朗玛峰的峰顶距离地球表面还要深2,000多米。

sentences.en: But it was a pretty good attempt, and the deepest known part of the trench, and the furthest known distance from the Earth’s surface is named after this ship and this expedition: Challenger Deep.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常好的尝试，海沟已知最深的部分以及距离地球表面最远的已知距离，都是以这艘船和这次探险命名的：挑战者深渊（Challenger Deep）。

sentences.en: And just as standing on the top of the world, and summiting Mount Everest has become a goal for the world’s most adventurous explorers, so has going to the very depths of the Mariana Trench.
sentences.zh: 正如站在世界之巅、登顶珠穆朗玛峰已成为世界上最具冒险精神的探险家的目标一样，前往马里亚纳海沟的最深处也是如此。

sentences.en: But compared to getting to the top of Mount Everest, getting to the bottom of the Mariana Trench is a lot harder.
sentences.zh: 但与登上珠穆朗玛峰的山顶相比，到达马里亚纳海沟的底部要困难得多。

sentences.en: The first people to achieve it were the American, Don Walsh, and his Swiss oceanographer colleague, Jacques Piccard, who managed it in 1960.
sentences.zh: 实现这一目标的第一批人是美国人唐·沃尔什（Don Walsh）和他的瑞士海洋学家同事雅克·皮卡德（Jacques Piccard），他们在1960年成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: This iconic descent took place in something called a Bathyscaphe, which looks a little bit like an airship, a Zeppelin, and consists of a small round pressure sphere at the bottom, where the two men would sit, and a large collection of tanks filled with gasoline in order to keep the device buoyant.
sentences.zh: 这次标志性的下潜是在一种叫做“里雅斯特号”深海潜水器（Bathyscaphe）的设备中进行的，它看起来有点像飞艇或齐柏林飞艇，由底部的圆形耐压球体（两名男子坐在那里）和一大批充满汽油的舱体组成，以保持装置的浮力。

sentences.en: The pressure sphere had to be incredibly strong, so it was made from reinforced steel 9 centimetres thick.
sentences.zh: 耐压球体必须极其坚固，因此它是由9厘米厚的增强钢制成的。

sentences.en: At those sorts of depths the pressure is so intense, it’s more than 1,000 times what it is at sea level.
sentences.zh: 在那种深度，压力极其巨大，是海平面上的1000多倍。

sentences.en: Or to put it another way, it’s like there was a 1,250 kilograms weight pushing down on every square centimetre of the craft.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像有1,250公斤的重量压在飞船的每平方厘米上一样。

sentences.en: There is absolutely no way a human body could withstand that sort of pressure; our organs would be instantly crushed, we would be compressed to a fraction of our normal size and, to state the obvious, instantly killed.
sentences.zh: 人类的身体绝对无法承受这种压力；我们的器官会被瞬间压碎，我们会压缩到正常体型的一小部分，显而易见，会瞬间死亡。

sentences.en: But, fortunately, the craft had been forged from incredibly strong steel, and the men successfully went to the depths of the Mariana trench and returned alive and well.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，这艘飞船是用极其坚固的钢材锻造的，这两个人成功地潜入了马里亚纳海沟的深处，并活着健康地返回了。

sentences.en: This was more than 60 years ago, but given the difficulty and expense of going so far deep, few others have managed it.
sentences.zh: 这已经是60多年前的事了，但鉴于下潜如此之深的难度和费用，极少有人再次做到这一点。

sentences.en: And as of a couple of years ago, there have been only 22 manned descents and 7 unmanned descents, so compared to the number of people who have climbed Mount Everest or even the number of people who have gone to space, it is still a tiny fraction.
sentences.zh: 截至几年前，只有22次载人下潜和7次无人下潜，所以与登上珠穆朗玛峰的人数甚至去过太空的人数相比，它仍然只占极小的一部分。

sentences.en: And, really, although we now have the technology to map the ocean floor without having to drop cannonballs and measure rope, and we can go anywhere in the ocean and have seen weird and wonderful deep sea creatures living at depths people once thought far too great to sustain life, the Earth’s seas and oceans are still among the worst-understood parts of the planet.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上，尽管我们现在拥有无需抛掷炮弹和测量绳索就能绘制海底地图的技术，并且我们可以去海洋的任何地方，并在人们曾认为压根无法维持生命的深度看到了奇怪而美妙的深海生物，但地球的海洋仍然是我们这个星球上了解最少的部分。

sentences.en: The legendary French maritime explorer and filmmaker Jean-Michel Cousteau once said that we understand the other side of the moon better than we understand our own oceans, so while we know more about it than ever before, the deep sea still is a comparative unknown that holds more questions than answers.
sentences.zh: 传奇的法国海洋探险家和电影制片人让-米歇尔·库斯托（Jean-Michel Cousteau）曾说过，我们对月球另一面的了解胜过对我们自己海洋的了解，所以尽管我们对它的了解比以往任何时候都多，但深海仍然是一个相对未知的领域，它带来的问题多于答案。

sentences.en: OK, that is it for today's episode on exploring the deep.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的深海探索节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, that you've learnt something new, and if you are going to a pub quiz and one of the questions is “which monarch was the first to travel underwater”, you will know the answer.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是一个有趣的节目，你学到了新东西，如果你要去参加酒吧问答，其中一个问题是“哪位君主是第一个在水下旅行的人”，你会知道答案。

sentences.en: King James I..
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯一世国王。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。
